alt_title: Diwali Gifts: When Tax Applies Under the New Income-tax Act
description: Money gifts from non-relatives, friends included, are taxable in full once they total more than ₹50,000 in a tax year: the whole sum, not the excess (Income-tax Act, 2025; the department's own example taxes all ₹53,000 of two gifts). A gifted TV is not counted. Gifts from relatives, and money received on your own marriage, are not taxed; Diwali is no exemption.

From an employer, gifts or vouchers below ₹15,000 in a tax year are valued at nil (Income-tax Rules, 2026; an older department page still shows ₹5,000 for gifts in kind). Receiving ₹2 lakh or more from one person in a day, or for one occasion, is allowed only through a bank, and a penalty can equal the sum. These are the department's rules as printed, not advice on anyone's tax.
question: Did you know the ₹50,000 rule?
x: Diwali gifts and tax (Income-tax Act, 2025): money gifts from non-relatives above ₹50,000 in a tax year are taxable in full. Relatives' gifts are not taxed. Employer gifts under ₹15,000 a year: nil value. Cash of ₹2 lakh+ from one person a day: bank only. Source: Income Tax Dept.
